key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual or sudden depending on cause. LOCATION: Generalized symptoms. DURATION: Continuous while bradycardic. CHARACTER: Lightheadedness, fatigue, weakness, syncope. AGGRAVATING: Exertion (symptoms worsen with fixed low heart rate). RELIEVING: Increased heart rate (pacing, medications). TIMING: Can be constant or episodic. SEVERITY: Variable, from asymptomatic to syncope. KEY POSITIVES: Heart rate <60 bpm with symptoms, syncope or near-syncope, fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, elderly patient, medications (beta-blockers, calcium blockers), prolonged PR or AV block on electrocardiogram (ECG). KEY NEGATIVES: NOT tachycardia, NOT palpitations.

includes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly
